The main text for the course is @hoffFirst2010 ([McMaster-accessible link](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-0-387-92407-6)) ([author's page](https://pdhoff.github.io/book/), with errata/code/data; [CrossValidated question about solutions manual](https://stats.stackexchange.com/q/44016/2126)

## Schedule

* worked through Hoff (approx 2 chapters/week), followed by
* probabilistic programming languages
* Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
* priors
* MCMC diagnostics (especially simulation-based calibration); parameterizations and priors for covariance matrices
* models for spatial and temporal data

## Miscellaneous refs/links


* Priors: @cromeNovel1996, @carpenterComputational2017, @gelmanPrior2006, @sarmaPrior2020, @bannerUse2020, @lemoineMoving2019, @kallioinenDetecting2022
* Pima Indians: @radinDigitalNativesHow2017, @smith-morrisReducingDiabetesIndian2004
* missing data: @vanbuuren2018, @harrell2015
* high dimensions/concentration of measure?

## Priors and parameterizations for covariance/correlation matrices

* @pinheiroUnconstrainedParametrizationsVariancecovariance1996a: unconstrained parameterizations of covariance matrices (Cholesky, log-Cholesky, matrix logarithm, ...)
* @lewandowskiGenerating2009a: the origin of the LKJ distribution on correlation matrices
* @chungNondegenerate2013a: weakly regularizing (boundary-avoiding) gamma priors on random-effect standard deviations
* rstanarm, ["Priors on covariance matrices"](https://mc-stan.org/rstanarm/articles/glmer.html#priors-on-covariance-matrices) (the `decov()` prior: covariance matrix decomposed into scale, simplex and LKJ correlation matrix)
* glmmTMB vignettes on [covariance structures](https://glmmtmb.github.io/glmmTMB/articles/covstruct.html) and [priors](https://glmmtmb.github.io/glmmTMB/articles/priors.html)
* @tokudaVisualizingDistributionsCovariance2025: visualizing distributions of covariance matrices (Wishart, inverse-Wishart, LKJ, ...); `VisCov` package

## MCMC diagnostics

We assume the basics (trace plots, R-hat, effective sample size). References in each subsection are ordered roughly from least to most technical.

### Divergences

* Stan, ["How to diagnose and resolve convergence problems: divergent transitions"](https://mc-stan.org/learn-stan/diagnostics-warnings.html#divergent-transitions-after-warmup) (what the warning means and what to try)
* bayesplot vignette, ["Visual MCMC diagnostics"](https://mc-stan.org/bayesplot/articles/visual-mcmc-diagnostics.html#divergent-transitions) (plotting where divergences occur)
* @betancourtDiagnosing2017 (the best single reference: the eight-schools funnel, why divergences signal biased inference, and how non-centred parameterization fixes it)
* @betancourtConceptual2017, section 6.2 (divergences in the theory of HMC; see also [Hamiltonian Monte Carlo](#hamiltonian-monte-carlo) below)

### Other diagnostics (e.g. R-hat)

* @vehtariRankNormalization2021a: rank-normalized, folded R-hat, bulk and tail ESS, rank plots (the version now used by Stan and the `posterior` package); the [online appendix](https://avehtari.github.io/rhat_ess/rhat_ess.html) has code and examples
* @vatsRevisiting2018: R-hat in terms of effective sample size, with a principled cutoff
* @margossianNested2025: nested R-hat, for running many short chains (`posterior::rhat_nested()`)
* @lambertRobust2022: R\*, a convergence diagnostic based on machine-learning classifiers
* @sailynojaGraphical2022: ECDF plots with simultaneous confidence bands, for rank plots and SBC (below)

### Simulation-based calibration (SBC)

* Stan User's Guide, ["Simulation-Based Calibration Checking"](https://mc-stan.org/docs/stan-users-guide/simulation-based-calibration.html) (begins with "Bayes is calibrated by construction")
* @nicenboimIntroduction2023, [section 10.2, "Validation of a computed posterior distribution"](https://bruno.nicenboim.me/bayescogsci/ch-custom.html#sec-validSBC) (includes an example where SBC finds a problem)
* The `SBC` R package (Modrák, Moon, Kim, Säilynoja): vignettes ["Getting started"](https://hyunjimoon.github.io/SBC/articles/SBC.html), ["Small model workflow"](https://hyunjimoon.github.io/SBC/articles/small_model_workflow.html), ["Limits of SBC"](https://hyunjimoon.github.io/SBC/articles/limits_of_SBC.html). Not on CRAN; install with `remotes::install_github("hyunjimoon/SBC")` or from [R-multiverse](https://r-multiverse.r-universe.dev/SBC).
* @schadPrincipled2021 (SBC as one step in a Bayesian workflow)
* @cookValidation2006 (the original idea)
* @taltsValidating2020 (the standard reference)
* @modrakSimulationBased2025 (the choice of test quantities, e.g. the joint likelihood, determines which problems SBC can detect)
* @sailynojaPosterior2026 (posterior SBC: checking calibration conditional on the observed data)

## Hamiltonian Monte Carlo

Roughly from least to most technical:

* Richard McElreath, ["Markov Chains: Why Walk When You Can Flow?"](https://elevanth.org/blog/2017/11/28/build-a-better-markov-chain/) (blog post with animations comparing Metropolis, Gibbs and HMC)
* Chi Feng, [interactive MCMC gallery](https://chi-feng.github.io/mcmc-demo/) (watch different samplers explore difficult target distributions in the browser)
* Alex Rogozhnikov, ["Hamiltonian Monte Carlo explained"](https://arogozhnikov.github.io/2016/12/19/markov_chain_monte_carlo.html) (interactive, light on maths)
* @betancourtConceptual2017 (conceptual rather than rigorous; sections 1–4 are the core)
* Michael Betancourt, ["Markov Chain Monte Carlo"](https://betanalpha.github.io/assets/case_studies/markov_chain_monte_carlo.html) (case study on MCMC in general and its diagnostics)
* @nealMCMC2011 (the standard technical reference; [arXiv preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.1901))

## Covariance/correlation parameterizations and priors

* @pinheiroUnconstrainedParametrizationsVariancecovariance1996a (unconstrained parameterizations of covariance matrices, e.g. Cholesky and log-Cholesky)
* @lewandowskiGenerating2009a (the paper behind the LKJ distribution on correlation matrices)
* @kristensenCovariance2026 (covariance structures available in `glmmTMB` and how they are parameterized)
* @gabryEstimating2026 (the `rstanarm` vignette on mixed models; its "Priors on covariance matrices" section explains the decomposition of covariance matrices used by `rstanarm`'s `decov()` prior)
* @tokudaVisualizingDistributionsCovariance2025 (visualizing distributions of covariance matrices)

## Simulation-based calibration

Roughly from friendliest to most technical:

* @modrakSBC2026: the `SBC` R package; start with the "Getting Started with SBC" vignette, which includes a deliberately broken model
* @stanSBC2026 (short chapter with a worked Stan example)
* @schadPrincipled2021 (SBC as one step in a Bayesian workflow, aimed at applied readers)
* @cookValidation2006 (the posterior-quantile predecessor of SBC; the core logic is easy to follow here)
* @gelmanBayesian2020 (brief conceptual discussion of SBC in the context of the overall workflow)
* @modrakSimulationBased2025 (re-explains SBC clearly; argues for checking derived quantities such as the log-likelihood, not just parameters)
* @taltsValidating2020 (the original rank-based SBC paper)

* Bayes in regulated industries: @greenlandDangers2026a, @leeEmbracingBayesianMethods2026

	* default `rstanarm` priors: [basic](https://cran.r-universe.dev/articles/rstanarm/priors.html), [covariance matrices](https://mc-stan.org/rstanarm/articles/glmer.html)

* measures of goodness-of-fit (WAIC, LOOIC, etc.): @gelmanUnderstandingPredictiveInformation2014, @hootenGuideBayesianModel2015, @vehtariCrossvalidationFAQ
* log-Gaussian Cox processes (standard model for spatial point processes)
* INLA (Integrated nested Laplace approximation), SPDE approaches
* variational inference: @bleiVariationalInferenceReview2017
